reasons.A: Short plain sentences and fragments with no contractions, close to the passage, but slips into more literary diction ('skinned with ice') and ends on a general reflection rather than a concrete observation.
reasons.B: Long, clause-heavy sentences, a semicolon and an abstract, essayistic stance ('Novelty makes you look at everything and see nothing') are far from the author's clipped, concrete plainness.
reasons.C: Best matches the clipped rhythm, flat plain diction and no-contraction register, with the same small self-correction move and a close on a bare concrete moment; only slightly more argumentative than the passage.
